note: Hand-maintained: questions, predictions, outcomes and decisions. Every number shown alongside comes from `uv run python -m epistemics.ledger build`, recomputed from frozen artifacts.

decisions.decision: The product is an epistemic passport: a consumer reading guide, not a paper.
Naturalistic tasks are the goal; formal tasks identify parameters and dossiers test transfer.
No fresh human data collection for at least several weeks; use published human benchmarks.
The core is a formal model with interpretable parameters (computational-psychiatry style), including an HGF volatility hierarchy and a value-of-certainty term.
HGF coupling kappa stays fixed; first modules T2, T3 and T5.
Do not capture reasoning summaries: model self-reports are dominated by response bias (Meyer, Garcia & Wulff 2026). Behaviour is the evidence.
No direct API runs for now; collections use the Codex CLI on the existing ChatGPT subscription.
Every reported table is regenerated by a versioned command from frozen artifacts (the ledger).

experiments.title: Compact delivery acceptance
experiments.question: Does one-call-per-checkpoint delivery work end to end and cut tokens?
experiments.outcome: Engineering and comprehension passed. Astra used about 22% fewer tokens; no saving established for Sol.

experiments.title: Research dossiers 0.1
experiments.question: Do agents neglect relays and selective disclosure when structure is stated in prose?
experiments.outcome: Astra and Sol matched the normative posterior in every arm; no neglect.

experiments.title: Research dossiers 0.2 (harder cues)
experiments.question: Does neglect appear when structure must be inferred from matching figures and a general fact?
experiments.outcome: No neglect; one repeated arithmetic slip by Sol on a control dossier.

experiments.title: Register versus validity
experiments.question: Are fabricated-but-polished reports weighted, and informal valid reports discounted?
experiments.outcome: Third null: fabrications ignored and informal reports fully weighted in every arm.

experiments.title: Positive control on 0.3
experiments.question: Does the battery separate weaker configurations at all?
experiments.prediction: If weaker configurations show neglect, the battery discriminates.
experiments.outcome: It discriminates: Luna took fabricated figures at face value unprompted and under-bought verification; Terra and Astra (low) missed the margin fabrication.

experiments.title: Disposition model recovery (T2, T3, T5)
experiments.question: Are the dependence prior, suspicion of silence and value of certainty identifiable?
experiments.outcome: Identifiable; T2 needs structure probes; certainty functions distinguishable at material values.

experiments.title: Disposition tasks acceptance
experiments.question: Which Bayesian are Astra and Sol when base rates are unstated?
experiments.outcome: Indifference Bayesians: every missing base rate set to 50%, exact updating, zero value of certainty; identical across retest and cover.

experiments.title: Model and tasks 0.2
experiments.question: Fix pricing issues; add framing, plausibility and learning variants.
experiments.outcome: All gates passed, including learning detection and start recovery.

experiments.title: Round 2: weaker configurations, framings, learning
experiments.question: Is the 50% default caused by wording, does knowledge move it, is it learned, and do weaker configurations differ?
experiments.outcome: Default survives open framing; Laplace learning from reveals; descriptions move priors, with Sol and Astra differing on disclosure; weaker configurations differ only in precision.

experiments.title: Description-to-prior modules 0.3
experiments.question: Can a five-level description-to-prior mapping be recovered, with stated against implied priors?
experiments.outcome: Recovered at r = 0.98-0.99; wall-clock timeout added.

experiments.title: Description-to-prior acceptance
experiments.question: How do Astra and Sol map graded source descriptions to priors?
experiments.outcome: Stated equals implied; irrelevant details ignored; shared relay mapping (5-95%); Astra ignored one disclosure description set entirely.

experiments.title: Description-to-prior retest
experiments.question: Are the mappings reliable across fresh contexts?
experiments.outcome: Disclosure mappings reproduce within 0.00-0.04 (Astra's set-B disregard is stable); relay extremes stable but the baseline moved from 50% to about 30% in one set.

experiments.title: What sets the relay baseline
experiments.question: Is the relay baseline a fixed default, anchored by early descriptions, or drawn afresh per context?
experiments.prediction: Fixed default: same first answer in identical-order repeats. Anchoring: irrelevant level lower after reassuring cases than after suggestive ones by at least 0.10 in both configurations. Stochastic: variation within identical orders as large as between orders.
experiments.outcome: No anchoring. Astra: fixed 50% default. Sol: 35-40% when asked cold, 50% after graded descriptions. Mild, ambiguous descriptions varied across contexts while extremes stayed fixed (the relative-judgement reading was later not confirmed).

experiments.title: Relative judgement of descriptions
experiments.question: Are ambiguous descriptions judged relative to the comparison set?
experiments.prediction: Relative judgement: mean target contrast (reassuring minus suggestive comparison set) of at least +0.10 in both configurations. Fixed mapping: within plus or minus 0.05.
experiments.outcome: Fixed mapping: mean contrasts -0.003 (Astra) and +0.016 (Sol). Relative judgement not supported. Ambiguous descriptions vary between contexts (up to 0.2 for Sol), independently of the comparison set.

experiments.title: Between-session variance of description priors
experiments.question: How much do priors from ambiguous source descriptions vary between fresh sessions, and is the variation a shared session shift?
experiments.prediction: P1: total between-session SD of the ambiguous levels at least 0.05 in both configurations. P2: the shared session shift is the larger component in both. No directional prediction between configurations.
experiments.outcome: P1 supported: between-session SD of ambiguous description priors 0.07 (Astra, moderate) and 0.11 (Sol, unstable by point estimate). P2 not supported: variation mostly level-specific. Astra's uninformative default fixed at 50%; Sol's ranged 22-52%, with one stated-implied divergence.

experiments.title: Weaker configurations on description modules
experiments.question: Do GPT-5.6 Luna and Terra map source descriptions to priors like the GPT-6 configurations?
experiments.prediction: W1: strongly suggestive above strongly reassuring by at least 0.30 in both modules. W2: median report noise above 0.05. W3: stated and implied within 0.10 at every level in at least 4 of 6 sessions per configuration.
experiments.outcome: W1 supported in 3 of 4 cells (Luna disclosure range only 0.22); W2 supported (median noise Luna 0.51, Terra 0.32); W3 supported for Terra (5/6) but not Luna (1/6): Luna states frontier-like base rates but its forecasts do not use them.

experiments.title: Dossier transfer of description priors
experiments.question: Do description-to-prior mappings measured in the formal modules predict answers when the same cases arrive as realistic document dossiers?
experiments.prediction: X1: dossier mapping within 0.10 of the formal mapping with rank agreement at least 0.8, for Astra and Sol in both modules. X2: own formal priors predict dossier answers better than 50% priors in all four cells. X3 (own versus pooled) exploratory.
experiments.outcome: Transfer holds: own formal priors predict dossier answers within 1.4-4.0 points versus 7.7-9.2 for 50% (X2 supported in all four cells); mappings differ by 0.025-0.060. X1's rank condition failed for relays (0.6, 0.7) because the middle levels are nearly tied; met for disclosure. Pooled priors do about as well as own. Dossiers were no less stable than the formal module.

experiments.title: Unprompted dossiers and weaker configurations on dossiers
experiments.question: Without being told that relaying or selective withholding exists, do agents discount copied reports and read silence as bad news when source descriptions suggest it? Do Luna's and Terra's formal mappings carry over to dossiers?
experiments.prediction: U1: strongly suggestive minus strongly reassuring implied prior at least 0.30 in all four Astra/Sol cells. U2: irrelevant level at most 0.20 (0.50 when prompted). U3: unprompted range smaller than prompted. U4 exploratory. W1: Luna/Terra own formal priors beat 50% on dossiers in all four cells. W2: Terra coherent in at least 4/6 dossier sessions, Luna in at most 2/6.
experiments.outcome: Mappings are conditional on the mechanism being named. Unprompted, Astra and Sol treated every matching report as independent, including an aggregator with no reporters (relay priors 0.00-0.03; full neglect, U1 fails) and read silence as only slightly bad news (disclosure range 0.22-0.23; U1 fails). Irrelevant level 0.00-0.02 (U2 supported); ranges shrank in all four cells (U3 supported); full neglect predicts unprompted forecasts best (0.2-4.5 points). Luna/Terra: relay mappings transfer, disclosure do not (W1 2/4); Terra coherence fell to 2/6 (W2 fails for Terra, holds for Luna at 0/6).
